Headline numbers: **Lockstep reproduces.** 2-value per-pixel at N=256: shared step 136.3, white 24.6, R2 steps 5.18, old VXGI IGN pair 131.6.
**Long run:** {S} is identical at frame 4×10⁹. Unwrapped float32 IGN degrades by 10⁵ frames; float Weyl and the old SSR analytic R2 break between 10⁶ and 10⁷.
Most surprising findings, mostly unfavou: **Per-pixel convergence comes from the Weyl steps, not from {S}.** A plain PCG hash + R_d steps, IGN + R_d and V&C + R_d all match {S} without a spatial filter (5.18 / 5.16 / 5.15 / 5.18).

**For two and four values per pixel, {S}'s hierarchy adds little over hash + R_d once a few frames are accumulated.** For two values it ties from about four frames on (EMA + blur is 14.2 for both). For four values it keeps a small lead, 4–14% depending on the window (about 14% at 32 frames). The clear leads are on a single frame (13–21% for two values, 11–18% for four) and for one value per pixel (25–53%).
**`R2_STEPS[0]` (0.7549, about 3/4) resonates with the base-4 hierarchy.** With that step {S} is 14% worse than a hash phase under EMA + 3×3; with every other step it is 10–38% better.
**IGN-based samplers beat {S} for one value per pixel with a blur.** Animated IGN: 1.5× under EMA, 1.7× on a single frame, 41% less flicker. IGN + golden Weyl also beats it by 18%.
**Against FAST,** {S}'s single-frame error is 34% (1-value) and 56% (2-value) higher, and its filtered flicker is 35–57% higher.

**The Three.js pull request's step usage is confirmed weak.** VXGI uses `R4_STEPS[0],[1]`; `R2_STEPS` is exported but unused. That costs 52% more per-pixel error at N=64 (24.6 vs 16.2) and nothing under EMA + 3×3 (17.0 vs 16.9), so only the unfiltered bake would benefit from R2. `R4_STEPS[0]` is about 6/7 and is 4.4× worse than golden as a 1-value sequence at N=64; `[3]` is about 7/13 and 6.3× worse at N=256. `R4_STEPS[0],[2]` puts samples on five visible lines (a₁ + 5a₂ is an integer to 0.0002).
**The old SSR analytic R2 is temporally red:** an EMA passes 2.7× more of its noise than white, and its four outputs are functions of one scalar.
**R4 is weak for 4 values per pixel:** L2 discrepancy is only 1.3× better than white at N=1024, and scrambled Sobol is 3.8× lower.
Methods as implemented: All samplers are in `noises.py` as `f(x, y, n, D)`. Integer paths use wrapping uint32; float paths use float32 for every operation.

**{S}:** three.js PR #35429 `HierarchicalHashedWeyl.js` verbatim. Seeds are k+1 per dimension. Steps are golden 2654435769 (1-value), `R2_STEPS` [3242174889, 2447445413] (2-value) and `R4_STEPS` [3679390609, 3152041523, 2700274805, 2313257605] (4-value). The pull request's constants equal round(2³²/gᵏ) to within 1.
**{S}, R4 steps 0-1:** what the Three.js pull request's VXGI actually evaluates, `bindHierarchicalHashedWeyl(res, 29).xy`, so seeds 117 and 118 with `R4_STEPS[0],[1]`.
**{S}, shared step:** golden step in every dimension.
**White:** three.js PCG nested as `pcg(x ^ pcg(y ^ pcg(n ^ pcg(d+1))))`, top 24 bits.

**Animated IGN:** `fract(52.9829189 * fract(0.06711056 p.x + 0.00583715 p.y))` with `p = pixel + 0.5 + float(n) * 5.588238 + offset_d`, in float32. Dimension 2 offset is (5.588238, 3.14159), the removed VXGI code. Dimensions 3 and 4 use (47, 17) and (101, 59), which are arbitrary choices. "64-cycle" is the removed VXGI code exactly (`n % 64`).

**Analytic R2 (old SSR):** `bindAnalyticNoise(res, 47)` from three.js dev, exactly. `index = n + 47`; `offset = floor(fract(float(index) * (0.7548776662, 0.5698402910)) * 32)`; `c = (pixel + offset) mod 32`. `t = c.x/P + c.y/P² + 47` with P = 1.32471795724474602596. Outputs are `fract(tP/P)`, `fract(2Pt/P²)`, `fract(3Pt * 0.4198754210)`, `fract(4Pt/P³)`.

**R_d Weyl + white offset / + IGN offset:** `fract(phase_d(x, y) + float(n) * α_d)` in float32. α is 1/φ for R1, 1/g and 1/g² for R2 with g = 1.3247179572, and 1/gᵏ for k = 1..4 for R4 with g = 1.1673039782614187 (root of x⁵ = x + 1). The fraction has 2²⁴/(nα) levels: 256 at n = 10⁵, 16 at 10⁶, 2 at 10⁷.

**V&C 64×64:** own Ulichney void-and-cluster texture (toroidal, σ 1.5, fixed seed), as `fract(tex[pixel + texelOffset_d] + float(n) * step)`. Texel offsets are (0,0), (23,41), (47,13), (11,53). Step is either golden for all dimensions ("shared") or R_d per dimension.

**STBN 128²×64:** from `NVIDIA-RTX/STBN` `Assets/STBN.zip`, 8-bit. Scalar for 1-value, vec2 for 2-value, vec2 twice at texel offset (49, 83) for 4-value. Slice is `n mod 64`, with a (37, 71) tile shift per cycle.
**FAST 128²×32:** the atlas from three.js PR #35244, read exactly as `FASTNoise.js` does. 1-value is the real texture, 2-value the vec2 texture, 4-value is xyzw.
**Bound:** scipy scrambled Sobol with an independent sequence per pixel.
A real GPU may fuse or reorder float operations, so the float methods follow shader source order rather than being bit-guaranteed.
Integrands: Defined in `integrands.py`; every stated mean is checked by Monte Carlo.

**2-value (14):** Smooth: uv, 0.5 + 0.5cos(2π(u−v)), 0.5 + 0.5cos(2π(u+v)), Gaussian bump σ 0.2. Edges: disc r = 0.4, quarter disc, u+v < 1, u < v, u+v < 0.7, box (u < 0.3 and v < 0.6), oblique 0.37u + 0.81v < 0.5. Rendering-like: cosine-hemisphere AO with a sinusoidal horizon, GGX (α 0.3) half-vector weighted by (h·l)⁸, GGX light hit h·l > 0.97.
**4-value (19):** Joint: mean(uᵢ), u1u2u3u4, Σuᵢ < 2, 4-ball r = 0.5, [u1<u3][u2<u4], SSR-like GGX(u1,u2)·[u3<0.4]·(0.5+u4), AO(u1,u2)·AO(u3,u4). Pairwise: uᵢ < uⱼ and uᵢ + uⱼ < 1 for all six pairs.
Group error is the RMS of the per-integrand RMSEs.
A. 1-value per-pixel convergence: Every golden-Weyl method shares one curve.
The textures beat white but fall at about N^−0.6 beyond their cycle length.
Analytic R2 is worse than white up to about N = 30.
Sobol is roughly 2× better than any Weyl sequence.

F. Spatial quality over time: Low-frequency share of the threshold mask's spectrum (below 1/8 cyc/px; white is 4.9%) at frames 0 / 1 / 7 / 100 / 10⁶:
The wrapped difference between neighbouring pixels never changes for {S}, V&C + Weyl or hash + Weyl (drift exactly 0).
It is 0.006 for scrolling IGN and 0.28 for STBN and FAST, the same as white (0.287).

So frame n of {S} is a different rank band of one static pattern. There is no best or worst frame, and the accumulated error is a fixed function of each pixel's phase, so its pattern stays blue-ish rather than white.
The cost is that the pattern cannot be co-optimised across frames, which shows up as the higher blurred flicker.
Consecutive-mask correlation is −0.43 for {S}, IGN and V&C (the minimum possible), −0.42 for STBN and −0.27 for FAST.

{S}'s steps are all odd, so each pixel has the full 2³² period (2.3 years at 60 fps) and the uint32 wrap is seamless.
STBN and FAST per-pixel sequences contain repeats: 57.5 and 59.7 distinct values per 64 frames.

The joint 4-value histogram for {S} is 0.54, more even than random.

X1. Bit-reversed rank pairing: An earlier experiment paired two dimensions inside each tile by bit-reversing the rank, and reported that per-pixel error barely changed while single-frame error nearly doubled. This section re-runs it. Dimension 1 is standard {S} with seed 1; dimension 2 is the bit reversal of dimension 1's 6-bit in-tile rank plus its own hashed tile phase (seed 2), so each tile holds the set (r/64, bitrev(r)/64), a (0,6,2)-net; temporal steps are `R2_STEPS` (`extras.py: hsn_bitrev`).
**"Per-pixel error barely changed" reproduces.** It is trivially true, because each pixel walks the same Weyl sequences.

**"Single-frame error nearly doubled" reproduces in direction.** The increase is 1.42× / 1.53× / 1.78× for the three filters, which leaves the variant worse than white. Edge integrands rise 1.57–2.07×; smooth ones improve slightly (0.89–0.92×).

**Cause:** bit reversal puts dimension 2's coarse bits at tile scale, so inside a small filter footprint dimension 2 is nearly constant. The benefit only appears for a filter covering exactly one tile, where it is 2.2× better (13× on smooth integrands).
X3. Step constants as Three.js uses them: Verified from the diff: VXGI uses `bindHierarchicalHashedWeyl(res, 29)` `.x` and `.y`, which are `R4_STEPS[0],[1]`. `R2_STEPS` is exported and unused by both effects. SSR uses all four R4 steps.

`R4_STEPS[0]` is confirmed poor: it is within 0.0005 of 6/7 (continued fraction [0; 1, 5, 1, 42, …]), so a pixel revisits seven clusters for about 300 frames. It is 4.4× golden at N=64 and 3.6× at N=256, yet best of all at exactly N=7.
`R4_STEPS[3]` is as bad: 6.3× golden at N=256.

**Would VXGI benefit from `R2_STEPS`?** Yes, measurably, for unfiltered accumulation: `R4[0],[1]` is 9% worse at N=16, 20% at 32, 52% at 64 and 24% at 256, and 10% worse under EMA with no blur. It is 8–12% better at N = 7–8. Under EMA + 3×3 blur there is no difference (17.0 vs 16.9). So the 64-sample light map bake is where it matters; real-time VXGI under TRAA would not show it.

**Visible lattice:** yes. `R4[0],[2]` gives five parallel lines through N=256 (scatter figure, third column), `R4[1],[3]` gives two diagonal bands at N=64, and `R4[0],[1]` shows columns at N=64. Only `R2_STEPS` looks unstructured at both counts.
R4 is the better choice for short histories and under EMA; the untuned set is 16–23% better at N ≥ 64.
X4. Is {S} needed? Hash + R_d (A) and IG: Both are implemented in uint32 fixed point with exactly {S}'s steps (`extras.py: hash_rd`, `ign_rd`). IGN offsets per dimension are (0,0), (47,17), (101,59), (173,113). The "R_d Weyl + white offset" and "+ IGN offset" rows in the main tables are the float-time versions and give the same numbers at small frame indices. The Sobol bound is a different, stronger reference and is not method A.
Per-pixel convergence is identical by construction (2-value, N=256: {S} 5.18, A 5.18, B 5.27).
{S} error divided by A or B (below 1.00 means {S} is better), at N = 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 / EMA 0.1:
**One value per pixel.** {S} beats the hash by 13–66%, but loses to IGN + golden at short histories: 73% worse on a single frame, 35% at four frames, 18% under EMA + 3×3.

**Two values.** {S} beats the hash only on a single frame (13–21%) and ties from four frames on. It beats the IGN phase by 9–29% with small blurs and 2–3× at σ2, because IGN phases at offsets are cross-correlated; the one exception is a 16-frame window, where B is 22% better.

**Four values.** {S} beats the hash by 11–18% on one frame and 4–9% at four frames, and keeps a small lead after that (4–14% depending on the window; about 14% at 32 frames, level at 16). It beats the IGN phase by 19–39% with small blurs and about 3× at σ2.
{S} is the only one of the three that is never the worst.
X5. Step and hierarchy resonance: This was one post-hoc diagnostic run; nothing was tuned as a result.
Ratio of {S} phase to hash phase for the same step(s), under EMA 0.1 + 3×3:

`R2_STEPS[0]` is about 3/4, and {S}'s top digit takes the values k/4 inside each 2×2 block. Stepping by about 3/4 nearly permutes the four pixels' values among themselves, so time adds little to what the spatial filter already averaged.
This is why the 2-value R2 configuration gains nothing over a hash under EMA + blur.
`R4[0],[3]` is 15% better than R2 under EMA + 3×3 (14.3 vs 16.9), despite being worse per pixel.
It suggests choosing steps jointly with the base-4 hierarchy; this was not explored.
Plain-language conclusions: **Where {S} matches blue noise textures**
One value per pixel under EMA + blur, on thresholded signals: within 3% of V&C and FAST, 11% better than STBN. On the smooth one-value integrands FAST is about 30% better and STBN about 14% better.
Temporal spectrum on thresholded signals: about level with STBN and FAST.
Every frame has the same spatial quality, and the accumulated residual stays blue-ish.
Four values per pixel: 7–12% better than stacked FAST or STBN.
Dimensions are independent across pixels.
**Where it falls short of them**
Single frame: 34% (1-value) and 56% (2-value) worse than FAST, with three times their low-frequency share.
Two values under EMA + blur: 25% behind FAST and 17% behind V&C + R2.
Blurred flicker: 35–57% above FAST and 15–19% above STBN.
The pattern only rotates, so it cannot be co-optimised across frames.
**Where it beats the alternatives**
White: 3.6× / 1.8× / 1.7× under EMA + blur for 1 values per pixel / 2-value / 4-value, and 9× / 4.7× / 2.6× per pixel at N=256.
Old VXGI IGN pair: 9.2× under EMA + blur and 25× per pixel.
Old SSR analytic R2: 1.3–1.4× under EMA + blur, 3× per pixel for 2 values per pixel, far better temporal spectrum and no float precision cliff.
Textures and IGN in unfiltered accumulation: 1.9× FAST and 3.1× STBN for 2 values per pixel at N=256.
Any frame index, with no wrap needed.
**Where it loses or ties**
IGN-based samplers for one value with a blur: animated IGN is 1.5× better under EMA, 1.7× on a single frame, with 41% less flicker.
IGN + golden Weyl for one value: 18% better.
Hash + R_d for two values: a tie from four frames on. For four values {S} keeps a small lead (4–14%).
Scrambled Sobol per pixel: 2.2× lower 2-value discrepancy at N=256, 3.8× lower for 4 values per pixel at N=1024.
Its own constants: `R4[0]` and `[3]` for 1 values per pixel, the `[0],[2]` pair, and `R2[0]` against the hierarchy.
Caveats and gaps: **Static flat field only.** There is no motion, reprojection, disocclusion or history clamping. Short reset histories are exactly where {S} is weakest against textures.
**One sample per pixel per frame.** Sharing the index between frames and several samples per frame is untested.
**No edge-aware or variable-footprint denoisers,** and no upscaling. Filter interaction with the 8×8 tile grid was only touched in X1.

**Aggregates are RMS over a hand-picked integrand set** with diagonal edges over-represented. Per-integrand tables are in `results/temporal/tables_AB.md` and `results/temporal/tables_D.md` for re-weighting.
**Texture animation is one common scheme each.** Random per-frame offsets and texel scrolling were not tested, and the textures are 8-bit.
**Some offsets are arbitrary choices:** IGN offsets for dimensions 3 and 4, and the V&C texel offsets.
**Float32 emulation follows source order,** so the large-frame results are precision-class rather than bit-exact predictions.

**Follow-on research worth doing:** steps chosen jointly with the hierarchy base (X5); a 2-value-aware spatial phase without the small-kernel penalty of bit reversal (X1); a better 4-value temporal component, such as integer Owen-scrambled Sobol or rank-1 lattices good in all projections; a real TAA resolve with motion and disocclusion; more than one sample per frame; perceptually weighted error.
EA's `noise.zip` was not downloaded; FAST comes from the PR #35244 atlas.
L∞ star discrepancy was not computed; L2 star is reported instead.
